items.prompt: createStatusReport gets a pageId the workspace owns, plus page component ids that belong to a DIFFERENT page of the same workspace. What does it throw?
items.answer: ConflictError, because the components' page differs from pageId
distractors: NotFoundError, because the components were looked up by pageId
ForbiddenError, as the components belong to another workspace
Nothing; the report is linked to whichever page the components use
items.explanation: After the page lookup, validatePageComponentIds checks the ids against the workspace and returns their page. If validated.pageId is not null and differs from input.pageId, the service throws ConflictError('pageId ... does not match the page ... of the selected components.'). Same-workspace components are not forbidden, and the report keeps input.pageId.

items.prompt: A dashboard user calls statusReport.create with a pageId from another workspace. Which tRPC error code reaches the client?
items.answer: NOT_FOUND, translated from the service's NotFoundError
distractors: FORBIDDEN, as the page belongs to a different workspace
BAD_REQUEST, as the input schema rejects the pageId
INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, since the insert hits a FK error
items.explanation: The service selects the page by id AND workspaceId and throws NotFoundError('page', ...) when nothing matches; toTRPCError maps the NOT_FOUND ServiceError code to TRPCError NOT_FOUND. The router test pins exactly that. No insert is attempted, and the id is a valid number for the schema.

items.prompt: notifyStatusReport runs for a workspace whose plan has limits['status-subscribers'] set to false. What happens?
items.answer: It returns quietly without dispatching anything to subscribers
distractors: It throws ForbiddenError, as the plan lacks subscriber support
It dispatches the update, as plan limits apply only in the UI
It queues the dispatch until the workspace upgrades its plan
items.explanation: After checking that the update belongs to the workspace, the function does if (!ctx.workspace.limits['status-subscribers']) return; before dispatchStatusReportUpdate. The comment says the silent skip matches emailRouter.sendStatusReport. ForbiddenError is thrown only when the update belongs to another workspace.

items.prompt: The dashboard calls the tRPC statusReport.list with { pageId, statuses: ['resolved'] }. Which reports come back?
items.answer: Reports of every status, as the router sends the service statuses: []
distractors: Only resolved reports, since the service filters on statuses
None at all, since an unknown input key makes zod throw an error
Only resolved ones, but capped at 100 by the service's limit
items.explanation: The router's zod object declares only period, order and pageId, so the extra key is stripped by default, and the call passes a fixed statuses: [], limit: 10_000, offset: 0. listStatusReports adds a status condition only when statuses.length > 0. The 100 cap belongs to the separate Connect handler. The guide says this test would fail today.

items.prompt: getEvents is called with both pageComponentId and monitorId. How does it choose which maintenances to include?
items.answer: By pageComponentId alone, with monitorId used only when it is absent
distractors: By monitorId alone, since it is the older, backward-compatible key
By either one, keeping maintenances that match pageComponentId or monitorId
By both, keeping only maintenances that match the two at once
items.explanation: The filter checks if (pageComponentId) first and returns its match; the monitorId branch runs only when pageComponentId is falsy, and with neither every maintenance is kept. The comment calls monitorId the backward-compatibility fallback.

items.prompt: A status-page component of type 'static' has incidents on record for the same monitor id. Which incidents does getEvents add for it?
items.answer: None, since incidents are added only when componentType is not static
distractors: Every incident from the last 45 days, as for any other component
Only unresolved incidents, shown with an error status on the page
Only incidents whose monitorId matches the component's monitor
items.explanation: The whole incidents block is wrapped in if (componentType !== 'static'); the comment says static components don't have incidents. The 45-day threshold and the monitorId filter apply only inside that block, for monitor-type components.

items.prompt: A status report's own status is 'investigating', and its latest update has status 'monitoring'. What event does getEvents produce for it?
items.answer: A degraded event that ends at the date of the monitoring update
distractors: A success event, as a monitoring update counts as recovery
A degraded event left open, with to kept null until it is resolved
No event, since only resolved reports appear in the feed
items.explanation: Only report.status === 'resolved' gives status 'success'. Otherwise the event is 'degraded' and to is lastUpdate.date when the last update's status is 'resolved' or 'monitoring', else null. So a monitoring update closes the bar's range while the report still shows as degraded.

items.prompt: pastDays is 45. A maintenance started 60 days ago, and an unresolved report's first update is also 60 days old. Which of them does getEvents include?
items.answer: Only the report; maintenances older than the threshold are dropped
distractors: Both, as getEvents applies no age limit to any of its event types
Neither, as both start before the 45-day threshold for the feed
Only the maintenance, since reports must be updated within 45 days
items.explanation: The maintenance loop returns early when maintenance.from < pastThreshod, and incidents check createdAt the same way. The reports branch deliberately skips the threshold; its comment says all unresolved reports are displayed. So the old report stays and the old maintenance goes.

items.prompt: statusPage.get sorts reports with a comparator meant to put reports without updates first. What is wrong with it when only b has no updates?
items.answer: It returns -1, ordering a first, when it should return 1
distractors: It returns 0, leaving the two reports in their original order
It throws, as it reads the last update of an empty array
Nothing; returning -1 there puts the empty report first
items.explanation: The comparator returns -1 if a has no updates (a first, correct) but also -1 if b has none, which puts a first again. The second check should return 1. Such an inconsistent comparator makes the order depend on the engine's sort algorithm, so empty reports are not reliably first; that check returns before the last-update read, so nothing throws.

items.prompt: assertSafeUrlSync is given http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/, the hex form of the IPv4-mapped 127.0.0.1. What does it do?
items.answer: Blocks it, since the hex pair is decoded back to 127.0.0.1
distractors: Allows it, since only the dotted ::ffff:127.0.0.1 form is checked
Blocks it, since every IPv6 literal is rejected outright
Allows it, since IPv6 hosts skip the private-address checks
items.explanation: isBlockedHost strips the brackets and calls isBlockedIPv6. For a ::ffff: prefix it first tries the dotted-quad form, then splits the hex pair 7f00:1 and rebuilds 127.0.0.1, which isBlockedIPv4 rejects. The comment notes Node's URL parser turns the dotted form into this hex form. Public IPv6 literals are allowed.

items.prompt: assertSafeUrl's docblock says it checks the resolved IP address. A public hostname whose DNS record points to 10.0.0.5 is passed in. What happens?
items.answer: It is allowed, as the code never resolves the hostname via DNS
distractors: It is blocked once a DNS lookup resolves the name to 10.0.0.5
It is blocked, since every hostname is first matched to an allowlist
It throws 'Invalid URL', since a private target is not a URL
items.explanation: Despite the docblock and the test comment 'async, with DNS resolution', assertSafeUrl only parses the URL, checks http/https, and calls isBlockedHost on the hostname string. There is no lookup, so a public name pointing at a private address passes. The code is keyed, not the comment; this is an open SSRF gap (DNS rebinding as well).

items.prompt: Workout 1 lists what createStatusReport writes on the happy path. Besides the status_report row, which rows does it create?
items.answer: An update row, a page-component link row, and two audit rows
distractors: An update row only, with the audit rows written by a later job
A page-component link row and one audit row for the report
An update row and a subscriber notification row for each user
items.explanation: The workout's behaviour block: status_report, status_report_update (the initial update), status_report_to_page_component (the association), and audit rows for the report and the update. Subscriber notification is a separate notifyStatusReport call, and audit is written in the same transaction, not later.

items.front: In the test-first lab, what does a router test prove that a service test does not, and what should it not repeat?
items.back: A router test proves the public API contract: that service rejections reach clients as the right TRPCError code (NotFoundError becomes NOT_FOUND) and that the procedure works end to end. It should not re-assert every association the service tests already cover.

items.front: Which categories of hostile input do the SSRF tests cover, and what testing pattern do they teach?
items.back: Allowed public URLs; blocked protocols (ftp, file, gopher, javascript, data); private IPv4; private hostnames (localhost, metadata hosts); private and IPv4-mapped IPv6; invalid URLs; the async variant. Pattern: a table of hostile examples looped into one it() per case, because safety code needs many bad inputs, not one happy path.

items.front: What does getEvents return, and which event types and statuses can it produce?
items.back: One list of events in a common shape { id, name, from, to, type, status }: maintenances (type maintenance, status info), incidents for non-static components (type incident, name Downtime, status error), and status reports (type report, status success if resolved, otherwise degraded).

items.front: What does the tRPC statusReport.create return, according to the router workout?
items.back: Not the report itself: it returns the initial status_report_update row with the caller's notifySubscribers flag spread into it ({ ...initialUpdate, notifySubscribers }), the shape the dashboard consumes. A caller that did not send the flag sees notifySubscribers undefined.
